method.rationale: Scope-preserving residual search: retain v003's inexpensive verification cascade, but make query-induced exclusions visible and use a bounded residual-coverage pass before stopping. Unlike a census anchor, source-bundle allocation, or cohort sampling, this targets silent narrowing of eligible subtypes and premature saturation. Parallel's observed 135 correct finds per dollar versus Exa's 56.8 supports retaining cheap probes, not assuming equivalent accuracy. The inspected incomplete attempt motivates the hypothesis but does not establish that it will recover its missing item.
method.instructions: Define X and Y exactly, including entity unit, exclusions, effective dates, eligible subtypes and group-membership rules. Start sequentially with one X-only search, one Y-only search and one conjunction search, using the user's broad predicate wording rather than a familiar subtype. Maintain deduplicated X/Y frontiers and an identity/evidence ledger. Also maintain a compact scope ledger: for each discovery query record added restrictions not required by the hunt (subtype, occupation, geography, era, source or familiar-name terms). A successful restricted query does not establish coverage of its parent category. Derive a few meaningful sibling partitions from source taxonomies or the eligibility definition; do not invent an exhaustive cross-product or enumerate a whole census by default. Run short discovery/check rounds, prioritizing expected verified additions per total resolution cost. Each round's neglected-subtype or reverse-frontier probe must address a specific untested scope-ledger cell or remove a recorded accidental restriction; merely paraphrasing a prior conjunction does not qualify. Check source-backed candidates on Parallel for only unresolved predicates, supplying identity and existing evidence. Use small affordable batches, price every candidate, and do not recheck established facts. No result means unresolved, not false; reject only on contradiction or an exhaustive applicable source. Escalate promising ambiguous or conflicting cases individually to Exa. After two discovery searches add no plausible identities, prohibit synonymous conjunction searches and perform a residual-scope pass: identify the most consequential restriction accumulated so far, try a sibling subtype or unrestricted parent on the opposite frontier, then resolve resulting candidates before further discovery. Reserve at least 35% of initial funds for evidence and stop discovery whenever pending checks require the remaining funds. Before submitting with spare funds, perform up to three affordable residual probes covering distinct untested restrictions or source partitions, retaining enough funds to verify their likely candidates. Stop this pass after two probes add neither candidates nor useful evidence; do not spend merely to exhaust the budget. Finish with identity, predicate, subtype and effective-date audits; submit supported intersections only and never infer completeness from saturation.
method.routing_rules: Parallel alone, default tier, 8 results for baseline and residual discovery, 4 for exact missing-fact checks. No routine also variants or broad auto-routing. Price candidate batches as the sum of queries and provider charges; fewer results are not presumed cheaper. Exa alone with 4 results for selected unresolved identities where ambiguity, conflicting evidence or inaccessibility warrants the higher cost. At most one initial Exa discovery probe after Parallel stagnation, continued only if it contributes useful new identities or evidence. Try a genuinely different scope partition on Parallel before buying provider diversity for a repetitive query. Authoritative-domain filters are for targeted evidence, not general frontier coverage; relax failed filters. Use publication-date filters only when publication date itself determines eligibility, and verify effective dates in content.
method.fetch_policy: Reuse cached source facts. Fetch authoritative pages that can settle missing identity or predicates, and useful multi-candidate lists, rather than every result. When a list is used for scope coverage, inspect its stated subtype, date range and pagination/section links; an excerpt or one section is not an exhausted category. Follow only sections tied to a promising uncovered partition, without committing to bulk census extraction. After a blocked or uninformative page, make one targeted alternate-source attempt rather than a fetch chain.

lessons.title: Provider attribution motivates a bounded challenger, not broad fusion
lessons.body: The supplied table attributes 143.9 correct finds per dollar to Parallel, 96.3 to Brave and 82.6 to Exa. These are observational totals, not marginal unique-find yields or controlled accuracy comparisons. They support retaining Parallel as default while testing one cost-capped Brave discovery challenge, measuring new verified identities rather than URL novelty. Search-result overlap literature provides a general motivation (https://bendersky.github.io/pubs/2010-5.pdf), not evidence of a Telem-specific gain. No improvement has yet been measured.
lessons.scope: Hypothesis: selective discovery-provider diversification under a fixed budget

failure_links.why: Repeated conjunction variants and familiar-name checks returned three of four items with funds remaining. This repeats incomplete coverage; the trace does not establish the identity or subtype of the missed item.
The already documented wrong submission followed searches containing an asserted match and a check of the other predicate. Link the existing weak-predicate failure rather than create another lesson.

candidates.title: Budgeted Challenger Discovery Probe
candidates.rationale: Preserve v007's scope-preserving cheap search, but distinguish scope stagnation from provider saturation using a bounded Brave challenger. Brave's attributed 96.3 correct finds per dollar exceeds Exa's 82.6, though neither establishes marginal value. Unlike broad routing or v009's stronger query admission rules, this tests an explicit alternative index at a controlled opportunity cost; verification remains on Parallel.
candidates.instructions: Define X and Y precisely, including entity unit, exclusions, eligible subtypes, group rules and effective dates. Start sequentially with one broad X-only, one broad Y-only and one conjunction search, without familiar-name or occupational narrowing. Maintain deduplicated X/Y frontiers, an identity/evidence ledger, and a scope ledger recording every added restriction. Derive a few meaningful partitions from source taxonomies, not an exhaustive cross-product. Choose the next frontier by expected verified additions per discovery-plus-resolution cost. Work in short discovery/check rounds; each round's reverse-frontier or neglected-subtype probe must remove a recorded restriction or address a genuinely untested partition. Check source-backed candidates only for missing predicates in small, individually priced batches. Supply established identity and evidence, not conjectured claims. Silence means unresolved, not false; reject only on contradictory evidence or an applicable exhaustive source. After two discovery searches add no plausible identities, stop conjunction paraphrases and run a genuinely different scope partition on Parallel. If that also adds no identities and the result sets mostly repeat already inspected evidence, consider one Brave challenge on the best unresolved broad frontier or source-derived partition. Do not use provider diversity to repeat a narrowed familiar-name query. Before buying it, compare its full cost plus likely checks with the best available Parallel probe; skip it when promising cheap checks or uncovered partitions dominate. Cap all Brave discovery charges at 15% of the initial budget, and buy no probe unless verification remains affordable. Immediately check its new source-backed identities on Parallel. A second Brave probe is allowed only after the first produces a newly verified intersection; new URLs, duplicate entities and unsupported names do not qualify. Continue normal Parallel scope search otherwise. Keep at least 35% of initial funds reserved for evidence; stop discovery when pending checks require the remainder. Before submission, perform up to three affordable residual probes of distinct untested restrictions, stopping after two produce neither candidates nor useful evidence. Audit identity, both predicates, subtype and effective date. Submit supported intersections only; saturation is not completeness.
candidates.routing_rules: Parallel alone, default tier, 8 results for baseline and residual discovery and 4 for missing-fact checks. Challenger: Brave alone, default tier, 8 results, subject to the 15% discovery-charge cap and outcome gate; it replaces, rather than supplements, routine Exa discovery. Exa alone with 4 results is reserved for promising individual verification cases with ambiguity, conflicts or inaccessible evidence. No auto-routing, routine also variants or multi-provider batches. Price every query and candidate at actual charges; do not presume fewer results cost less. Count discovery plus follow-up verification when evaluating challenger yield, and do not credit duplicate finds to marginal gain. Domain filters are for targeted evidence, relaxed after failure, not general coverage. Publication-date filters only when publication date determines eligibility; otherwise verify effective dates in content.
candidates.fetch_policy: Reuse cached source facts. Fetch authoritative pages that settle missing predicates or identity, and useful multi-candidate lists. Inspect scope, date ranges and pagination before claiming list coverage; follow only promising uncovered sections. Fetch Brave-discovered evidence under the same standards as Parallel evidence, not merely because it comes from a new provider. An engine summary or repeated assertion is not independent proof. After a blocked or uninformative fetch, make one targeted alternate-source attempt rather than a fetch chain.

candidates.title: Source Grounded Bridge Expansion
candidates.rationale: Keep v007's routing and scope safeguards, but add a conditional discovery path for predicates expressed through intermediate entities rather than the requested person's name. Search source-backed group, work, event or record relationships before guessing more familiar people. This is neither a census join nor blanket source-bundle allocation: it expands only eligibility-relevant relation paths. Multi-hop retrieval literature motivates the mechanism (https://aclanthology.org/2023.findings-acl.657.pdf); the inspected logs show group-credit and alias cases but do not establish an incremental recall gain.
candidates.instructions: Define X and Y exactly, including requested entity unit, exclusions, subtypes, group-membership rules and effective dates. Start sequentially with broad X-only, Y-only and conjunction searches. Maintain deduplicated frontiers, identity/evidence and scope ledgers as in v007: record accidental restrictions, derive a few source-backed sibling partitions, and never treat restricted success as parent-category coverage. Add a compact relation ledger only when sources show that a predicate is recorded on a different entity unit: for example a qualifying group, credited work, event, institution or named record linked to the requested entity. Record the intermediate entity, the explicit relationship, source, applicable date and missing edge. Treat shared names as identity questions, not relationships. After the baseline, ask whether either frontier systematically hides eligible entities behind such a relationship. If so, substitute one source-grounded bridge probe for a normal discovery probe: retrieve the qualifying intermediate entity's explicit recipients, named members, creators or other eligibility-relevant roster, and bring newly identified requested-unit entities into the frontier. A confirmed find may supply a bridge lead, but do not infer that its associates qualify. Expand only relationships permitted by the hunt, at most one intermediate entity between the requested entity and each predicate; do not crawl arbitrary collaborators or biographies. Select one promising bridge at a time and check at most three new identities before expanding further. Prefer paths that establish one predicate for several new identities and leave only one inexpensive check each. Stop a bridge family after two probes add neither source-backed candidates nor useful missing-edge evidence; return to ordinary opposite-frontier or residual-scope discovery. No bridge is mandatory when the source structure provides no justification. Run small discovery/check rounds prioritized by total resolution cost, with a genuine neglected-scope probe each round. Check only unresolved predicates and identity edges, preserving established facts. Group membership or work association does not automatically transfer an award or status: require the hunt's exact qualifying relationship and date. Silence remains unresolved. After two unproductive discovery searches, prohibit synonymous conjunction searches and try an untested sibling or unrestricted parent on the opposite frontier, or an evidenced untested relation path. Reserve at least 35% of initial funds for checks; stop discovery when pending checks consume the remainder. Perform up to three affordable final residual probes on distinct untested restrictions or relation paths, stopping after two without candidates or useful evidence. Submit only deduplicated entities with both predicates and every required identity or relationship edge supported.
candidates.routing_rules: Parallel alone, default tier, 8 results for baseline, bridge and residual discovery; 4 for exact missing-edge checks and check_candidates. Use verified intermediate-entity names and neutral relationship questions, not asserted eligibility. Price each candidate and query separately, including downstream relationship checks. No routine also variants, auto-routing or multi-provider requests. Escalate only promising ambiguous, conflicting or inaccessible individual cases to Exa alone with 4 results. At most one initial Exa discovery probe after genuinely different Parallel scope or relation partitions stagnate, continued only if it adds useful identities or evidence. Domain-filter targeted roster, credit or authoritative-record checks, not broad frontier coverage; relax failed filters. Publication-date filters apply only when publication date defines eligibility; check relationship and status effective dates in content.
candidates.fetch_policy: Reuse cached evidence. Prefer fetching the specific roster, credit table, namesake origin or record section that can expose and support a missing relation edge. Inspect its entity unit, inclusion rules, dates and relevant pagination before treating it as covered. Extract explicit identities rather than guessed associates, and preserve the source supporting each edge. Fetch authoritative missing-predicate pages when needed; do not fetch every result or enumerate a whole institutional census. After a blocked or uninformative page, try one targeted alternate source. No acceptance based solely on a generated relationship summary or an uninspected plausible URL.
